z-m-33-01.title: Three vertices given: the last one na just one point?
z-m-33-01.topic: Finding the last vertex of parallelogram when three vertices given
z-m-33-01.goal: Decide if last vertex of parallelogram must be one point when only three known. Explain why e no fixed and what extra info needed (vertex order), then find all possible points yourself.

Choose point D to make A, B, C, D vertices of one parallelogram. Original task only say “let fourth vertex be D”; e no say order to connect vertices. All coordinates real, and all four points different.

z-m-33-02.title: If one line appear, does it mean the two circles meet?
z-m-33-02.topic: Position of two circles and line wey come from their equations
z-m-33-02.goal: Use examples to check that equations of two circles fit give a line even when circles no meet. Make two circles yourself wey no meet and explain wetin else need checking.
z-m-33-02.material: Circle C1 equation na x²+y²=4 (center (0, 0), radius 2). Read as “x squared plus y squared equals 4”. Circle C2 center (d, 0), radius r, with d>0, r>0; equation (x-d)²+y²=r². Hayun subtract C2 equation from C1 and get first-degree expression in x, then say, “Line come out, so two circles meet at the two points on this line.” Here, circles meet means one point belongs to both (including touching).
